visual: Compact spreading evergreen with large aromatic green leaves and dense conical clusters of strongly fragrant creamy green to greenish-yellow flowers in spring.
water: Keep moderately moist but well drained; water containers and newly planted specimens during dry spells.
soilWarning: Hot dry sun scorches and yellows leaves
prune: Requires little routine pruning; remove damaged or misplaced shoots after flowering if necessary.
toxicity: Skimmia fruit is considered ornamental and should not be eaten, although this male cultivar does not itself produce berries.
resilience: Hardy, shade tolerant and relatively tolerant of atmospheric pollution and neglect once established.
uses: Shady borders, woodland gardens, fragrant spring planting, evergreen structure, containers and pollinating female Skimmias.
uncertain: 'Kew Green' is a male cultivar and therefore does not produce its own berries; it can pollinate compatible female Skimmias.
